transcript.text: fridge part freezin stuff, lettuce + yoghurts frozen solid at the back. hotpoint ff. any ideas pls

This is usually caused by food sitting directly against the cold back wall or in front of the air vent. Move your lettuce and yoghurts forward so there is a gap between them and the rear panel; they should thaw out quickly if that was the only issue. If moving the food doesn't help, it could be a defrost fault where ice has built up behind the back panel, blocking airflow. To check this, you would need to unplug the fridge for 24 hours with doors open to let any hidden ice melt completely. If the problem returns after that, we likely have a failed defrost part (like the heater or thermostat) which requires an engineer.

ok moved stuff forward, it's absolutely rammed after a big shop and things were pressed right against the vent slots at the back. don't really want to unplug it for 24hrs with all the food in. anything else to try first?

Since moving the food hasn't stopped the freezing, the next most likely cause is that the defrost drain at the bottom of the back wall is blocked with ice or debris. This prevents meltwater from draining away, causing it to refreeze and block airflow, which makes the fridge compartment too cold. Please check if that small drain hole is clear by gently pouring a little warm water into it; if it flows away freely, the issue might be a deeper defrost system fault requiring an engineer.
not sure where the drain hole is tbh, cant see one at the back. where would it be? it's a frost free if that matters

On most Hotpoint frost-free models, the drain hole is located at the very bottom of the fridge compartment's back wall. It often sits behind a small plastic cover or grille that can be gently pried off with a flat-head screwdriver (ensure it is switched off first). Can you check if there is a small hole or channel right at the bottom rear, and whether it looks clear?
cant see any hole or cover at the bottom back tbh, not sure what im looking for. also the dial was turned right up to max, think one of the kids moved it. what should i do with that?

That explains it perfectly: turning a dial to 'max' makes the fridge run as cold as possible, which will freeze items like lettuce and yoghurts sitting against the back wall. Leave it like this for 24 hours with the doors shut; if the frozen items thaw out and stay fresh, that was the only problem.
